title: Marcos seeks action on illegal, unregulated fishing at APEC
summary: SHENZHEN - President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. raised the matter of illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing during the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.

blocks.text: SHENZHEN – President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. raised the matter of illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing during the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.
The Philippine leader sought concerted action against questionable fishing practices, according to the Presidential Communications Office (PCO).
Marcos likewise pushed for the digital transformation of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) through artificial intelligence and a charter for a sustainable blue economy,

The president also reaffirmed the Philippines' support for the rules-based multilateral trading system and highlighted the conclusion of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement under the country’s chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in 2026.

He said that APEC discussions “must translate into real benefits for the people” through job creation, better access to healthcare, and preparation for demographic change and a growing silver economy.
Also on Thursday, the Philippines and Chile on Thursday formally signed their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
The signing was led by Marcos and Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast during a bilateral meeting held at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center.
Marcos said the signing of the free trade deal was something that the Philippines "very much hoped for."
"We're very happy that we have finally come to a formal agreement," the Philippine President said.

"The FTA is going to provide us with a very, very important foundation to build on to make this trade, this relationship, not only in trade, not only between governments, but between our people—stronger, more vibrant, and deeper," he added.
Marcos and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori also on Thursday discussed the possibility of establishing a joint trade commission to advance bilateral trade.

The PCO said that Marcos and Fujimori also talked about exploring cooperation in environmental protection and disaster risk reduction and management amid the threat of a super El Niño that is expected to affect both countries.

During the bilateral meeting, the two leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties and advancing cooperation in areas of mutual interest. –Giselle Ombay/NB, GMA News
